title: Quadrilateral properties
examples: What is the difference between a parallelogram and a rhombus?
If one angle is 70 degrees, what are the others?
Can a kite also be a rhombus?

explain.say: Today we explore special four-sided shapes called quadrilaterals. A parallelogram is a shape with two pairs of parallel sides. Opposite sides must be equal in length too.

items: Parallelogram: two pairs of parallel sides

draw.text: Parallelogram: Two pairs of parallel sides.

explain.say: Next we look at the rhombus. A rhombus is a parallelogram where all four sides are equal in length. Think of a square tilted on its corner.
A trapezium, sometimes called a trapezoid, has only one pair of parallel sides. This is its defining feature you must remember.

draw.text: Trapezium: Exactly one pair of parallel sides.

explain.say: Finally, consider the kite. A kite has two pairs of equal-length sides that are next to each other. Its diagonals are perpendicular.

draw.text: Kite: Two pairs of adjacent equal sides.

faq.q: Can a square be any of these shapes?
faq.a: Yes, a square is a very special shape. It is a parallelogram, a rhombus, and even a rectangle. It fits many definitions.
asks: Does a square have all those properties?

faq.q: What if a shape has three pairs of parallel sides?
faq.a: That is impossible for a standard quadrilateral. The maximum number of parallel sides it can have is two pairs.
asks: Can a shape have more than two parallel sides?
What is the limit on parallel sides?

faq.q: Does a rhombus always have right angles?
faq.a: No, a rhombus only has right angles if it is also a square. Otherwise, its angles can be different.
asks: Must a rhombus be a square?
Are the angles always 90 degrees in a rhombus?

faq.q: Is it possible for a kite to be a parallelogram?
faq.a: Yes, if a kite has opposite sides equal, it becomes a parallelogram. In that case, it must be a rhombus.
asks: Can a kite be a parallelogram?
What makes a kite into a parallelogram?

faq.q: What is the main difference between a trapezium and a parallelogram?
faq.a: The key difference is the number of parallel sides. A parallelogram has two pairs, while a trapezium has exactly one pair.
asks: How many parallel sides must a parallelogram have?
Does a trapezium always have parallel sides?

facts: A parallelogram has opposite angles that are equal in measure.
A rhombus has four sides of equal length.
A trapezium has at least one pair of parallel sides.
The diagonals of a kite are perpendicular to each other.

quiz.say: A shape has opposite sides parallel and all four sides equal. What is it?
quiz.why: A rhombus fits the definition of having all four sides equal, which is a key feature.

wrong.1: A parallelogram only needs opposite sides parallel, not necessarily all sides equal.
wrong.2: A trapezium only requires one pair of parallel sides, not all sides equal.
wrong.3: A kite only requires two pairs of adjacent equal sides, not necessarily all four equal.

quiz.say: Which shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
quiz.show: Exactly one pair of parallel sides.
quiz.why: The definition of a trapezium is having precisely one pair of parallel sides.

wrong.0: A kite does not have to have any parallel sides at all.
wrong.2: A parallelogram must have two pairs of parallel sides.
wrong.3: A rhombus is a type of parallelogram, so it has two pairs of parallel sides.

quiz.say: If a quadrilateral has two pairs of adjacent equal sides, what is it called?
quiz.show: Two pairs of adjacent equal sides.
quiz.why: The specific property of two pairs of equal sides next to each other defines a kite.

wrong.1: A rhombus requires all four sides to be equal, which is a stricter condition.
wrong.2: A parallelogram focuses on opposite sides being parallel, not adjacent sides being equal.
wrong.3: A trapezium's defining feature is only one pair of parallel sides.
